question: How large are the train and test set of CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and did the authors apply augmentations to their experiments?
answer: The authors state that both CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 consist of 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images (1). They explicitly note that no data augmentation was used for either dataset in their experiments, apart from the input dropout itself (2).

sources.quote: B.3 CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 The CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 data sets consists of 50,000 training and 10,000 test images each. They have 10 and 100 image categories respectively. These are 32 × 32 color images. We used 5,000 of the training images for validation. We followed the procedure similar to MNIST, where we found the best hyperparameters using the validation set and then combined it with the training set. The images were preprocessed by doing global contrast normalization in each color channel followed by ZCA whitening. Global contrast normalization means that for image and each color channel in that image, we compute the mean of the pixel intensities and subtract it from the channel.

Goodfellow et al. (2013) showed that the error is further reduced to 11.68% by replacing ReLU units with maxout units. On CIFAR-100, dropout reduces the error from 43.48% to 37.20% which is a huge improvement. No data augmentation was used for either data set (apart from the input dropout).
